A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPG-SAM 2 work, and all supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v3 includes supplementary Sections A–B; v2 mentions an appendix but contains none. The supplied content supports reliable comparison without establishing when the supplementary experiments were performed.

before.justification: v2 reports original RVOS benchmark evaluations and component/configuration ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and includes additional loss-transfer, model-size and fusion-ablation results in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same multimodal encoder, mask prior generator, global-historical aggregator, prompting procedure and combined training loss. The supplementary experiments test existing components and alternative model configurations without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17 and MeViS for evaluation and RefCOCO/+/g for the stated pretraining. The supplementary examples come from retained benchmarks and do not introduce a different task, population or input-processing scenario.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. v3 adds HyperSeg to the reported parameter/performance comparison in Table 6. Table 5 also compares existing ReferFormer and SgMg models with variants using the proposed similarity loss.

E3.justification: The main training schedules, splits, metrics and settings remain unchanged. Appendix A adds a SAM 2-Hiera-Large/BEiT-3-Base Tiny configuration, loss-transfer comparisons using ReferFormer with ResNet-50 and SgMg with Video-Swin-T, and HGA component controls and one-to-three-layer sweeps.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's aggregate component and configuration studies, Tables 5–8 add cross-model loss transfer, full-model loss removal, parameter/performance analysis, separate HGA fusion-part ablations and depth sensitivity. Figure 5 adds qualitative cases involving occlusion, multiple targets, similar objects and shadows. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The additional supplementary results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, including MPG-SAM 2's 73.9, 72.4 and 53.7 J&F benchmark scores. New Table 5 reports paired loss comparisons of 55.6 versus 56.4 for ReferFormer/ResNet-50 and 62.0 versus 62.8 for SgMg/Video-Swin-T. Table 6 adds Tiny's 69.9 J&F at 0.46B parameters; Tables 7–8 and Figure 5 add fusion, depth and qualitative findings. This substantially expands reported results while retaining the original outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and their mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The supplement adds empirical studies and interpretations, without new or revised formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about mask-prior prompting, global-historical aggregation, temporal consistency and benchmark superiority. The supplementary evidence does not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations concerning loss transferability, accuracy relative to parameter count, and redundant information from deeper fusion modules. Appendix B interprets selected visual examples as evidence of robustness to occlusion and distractors. The earlier interpretations remain, and no substantive failure-condition or limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and documents the Tiny model's initialization, supplementary comparator backbones and total parameter counts. The existing hardware, learning rates, training schedules and preprocessing details remain unchanged. Repository accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Unified Embedding Alignment, Semantic and Sequential Alignment, LogicZSL and HyperSeg. Appendix A additionally positions MPG-SAM 2 against HyperSeg on model size and reported performance. The established related-work narrative and earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence are almost unchanged. v3 compacts author affiliations, removes the displayed email addresses, adds the code-access sentence, changes a cross-reference in Section 3.4, and inserts supplementary Sections A–B before the references. There is no extensive rewriting of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary displays for loss transfer, parameter/performance comparisons, fusion-component and depth ablations in Tables 5–8, plus the four-case video visualization in Figure 5. These substantially expand the visual evidence. Existing Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 are retained, with table placement and page layout reflowed around the compacted title block.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the existing method through loss-transfer tests, finer HGA ablations and parameter/performance evidence in Tables 5–8, supplying analysis that v2's appendix pointer did not provide. The code link improves reproducibility information. These are useful supporting gains while the principal method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged; uncertainty estimates are still absent for the added small performance differences.
